entries.contract: Season spans are Dawn days 0–11, Highsummer 12–23, Ember 24–35, and Hush 36–47, then repeat.
Daily moisture smoothing uses the previous day’s grid so results do not depend on traversal order.
Plant comfort uses effective shade, including nearby cloth.
Bare soil gains one nutrient each day before habitat aftercare.
Low-vitality plants recover two nutrients only when their resulting vitality is below 25.
Glowcaps die after age 75; ordinary plants die after age 105.
Hush reduces comfort by two for every species except glowcap.
Shade cloth adds shade to its tile and all four orthogonal neighbors.
Rain barrels add six moisture only on days with rainfall.
Fireflies equal half the healthy glowcap count rounded down.
Worm census includes both soil and peat cells.
A tile that had mulch at the start of aftercare receives its third-day nutrient benefit even if that point decays that day.
Stress rises only below vitality 30; vitality 30 reduces stress by three.
Rectangle selection includes both horizontal corners.
Circle brushes include points whose squared Euclidean distance is at most the radius squared.
Transplant moves stress from the source tile to the destination tile.
Pruning never makes plant age negative.
Pruning caps vitality at 100.
Harvest resets age to zero, preventing an immediate repeat harvest.
Crafting verifies the total inputs for every requested batch before changing inventory.
Watering a living nursery batch restores hydration to three days.
Each hydrated nursery day adds three vitality, including for ready batches.
A dry day removes vitality but does not advance nursery age.
Planting one nursery member costs four nutrients.
Bed names are unique without regard to case.
A care plan can be scheduled for tomorrow, the first day after the current day.
A completed plan decrements its remaining run count and updates status after the atomic tile edit.
An overdue imported plan executes on the next step.
All daily rule conditions use one shared snapshot taken before any rule actions.
A year contains 48 days, so phase returns a zero-based day position from 0 through 47.
Census coverage is a percentage rounded to two decimal places.
Average vitality includes living plants only.
Diversity is natural-log Shannon entropy.
Suitability scores use effective shade including cloth structures.
Recommendations omit occupied tiles by default and include them when empty_only=False.
Stress alerts trigger at 50 and above.
Patch groups sort by size descending then topmost and leftmost.
Transects use the integer Bresenham line including both endpoints.
Forecast timeline always includes the final day.
Tag searches match one normalized tag exactly.
Date search includes both endpoints.
Specimens capture every field of the living cell.
Overdue tasks have due days strictly before today.
Task completion can be toggled back to open.
Task lists sort by due day then ID.
Calendar day zero is Dawn day 1.
Weather wetness probability follows the season for the requested day.
Almanacs report longest consecutive clear spell.
next_weather searches future days starting tomorrow.
Calendar expands only the remaining finite plan occurrences.
Each experiment event executes once at its exact offset.
Experiment samples include the final day.
Treatment differences are measured against control.
Experiment ranking preserves branch order for ties.
Treatment names are unique without regard to case.
CSV import publishes exactly one revision.
Blueprint mirroring reflects each x coordinate across the rectangle.
Blueprint rotation maps coordinates into the rotated dimensions.
Markdown task checkboxes appear in due-day order.
Color scale interpolation rounds intermediate channels.
Shade maps display effective shade, including nearby cloth.
History chart x positions use actual day spacing.

BEHAVIORS 121: a new edit after undo clears the obsolete redo branch.
BEHAVIORS 120: revision checks require equality, including future revisions.

COURIER.md: causal vectors treat absent components as zero; independent writers are incomparable.
COURIER.md: a resumed writer must advance beyond all of its already observed sequences.
COURIER.md: field values remain owned by the caller and cannot modify issued events later.
COURIER.md: reused writer sequences with different content are rejected.
COURIER.md: concurrent edits survive deletion; a later observed deletion hides a record.
COURIER.md: concurrent distinct authored text values are preserved exactly and case sensitively.
COURIER.md: omission contexts are per record; an observation of one record does not delete another.
COURIER.md: projection shares neither values nor omission context for unselected records.
COURIER.md: the acknowledged frontier has been seen by every active device, with missing acknowledgements zero.
COURIER.md: receiving a projection for Q advances writer allocation clocks but does not establish causal knowledge of delayed R edits. Both edit and checkpoint contexts use per-record coverage.
CAMPAIGNS.md: every resumed or replayed branch uses its recorded simulation release; opting into a new release requires an explicit fork.
CAMPAIGNS.md: a replaced worker cannot publish after another generation has reclaimed its branch.
CAMPAIGNS.md: a checkpoint contains all events at its offset, and a continuation inherits only strictly later events.
CAMPAIGNS.md: compaction retains every checkpoint referenced by an immutable descendant lineage.
CAMPAIGNS.md: branch progress, immutable checkpoint and terminal report publish in one transaction.
HISTORY.md object references: correction replays resolve the original logical object even when local IDs are reassigned.
HISTORY.md: replay checkpoints require the complete preceding authored history and interpreter identity to match.
HISTORY.md: shared authored events apply once; separately authored equal actions both apply during cherry-pick.
HISTORY.md: three-way rebase compares against the immutable revision recorded when the child forked.
HISTORY.md corrections: replacement integer IDs bind in the original event's preceding state, including objects deleted later in the same history.
HISTORY.md shared insertions: rebase preserves both sides' authored order, merges compatible constraints, and reports order-conflict when the same shared events impose a cycle.
HISTORY.md rebase: original numeric bindings are audit metadata; a binding change for the same logical reference and command is not a different authored edit.
ENSEMBLES.md: each visible result identifies one immutable input snapshot; publication validates all actual reads, including newly selected plans.
ENSEMBLES.md: treatment/control comparisons use the same source identity and elapsed sample offset; failed members are excluded only from their own pair.
ENSEMBLES.md: report ID --revision N returns exactly the previously published immutable envelope after edits and restarts.
ENSEMBLES.md: numerical cache origin is diagnostic; requested replicate/treatment identity is preserved, including equal-valued saved sources.
SAVE_MERGE.md: only ancestor identifiers have common identity; independent post-fork allocations survive even when their local numbers and contents match.

Offline publication reconciliation must compare all latest common observations; independent merges followed by independent reverts preserve both reverts. Complete parcels retain the ancestry needed to do so.
STUDIES.md: final promotion waits for every stage trial to succeed or fail; partial common-cohort rankings are provisional previews only.
STUDIES.md: a promoted trial resumes from its own complete checkpoint identified by study, stage, source and treatment; control is a separate trajectory.
FIELD_CALIBRATION.md: timestamp origin does not change calibration or staged study outputs.
WORKSPACE_CATALOG.md: upgraded and fresh catalogs use the same Unicode compatibility and whitespace label matching while retaining all receipts.
IRRIGATION.md: each valve configuration receives a maximum feasible integral delivery under directed capacities, outlet demands and remaining supply.
IRRIGATION.md: solve returns a global optimum in final total vitality, with remaining tank supply as a tie breaker, over the finite supplied valve schedules.
